ap_computer_science_a-f02.title: RunFinder: the longest run in an ArrayList

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Write the method longestRun, which returns the length of the longest run of consecutive equal values in the ArrayList data. A run is a sequence of one or more neighboring elements that are equal. The method returns 0 if data is empty and must not modify data. For example, if data is [1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 3] the method returns 3, and if data is [4, 5, 6] the method returns 1. Complete the method longestRun.

rubric_rows.criterion: Handles an empty list by returning 0 without an exception
Traverses the list with correct bounds so every neighboring pair is examined (indexes stay inside the list)
common_errors: reads data.get(i + 1) at the last index

rubric_rows.criterion: Compares each value with its neighbor (previous or next element), not with the first element
Compares Integer values with equals (or by unboxing), not with == on objects
Extends the current run length when the values are equal
Restarts the current run length at 1 when the values differ
Keeps the maximum run length seen so far (updates it when a run is longer)
Initializes the counters so a list with one element returns 1
Returns the best length after the traversal and does not modify data

ap_computer_science_a-f03.title: WordFilter: remove short Strings from an ArrayList

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Write the method removeShort, which removes from the ArrayList words every String whose length is less than minLength. The order of the remaining Strings must not change, and the method changes the list it is given rather than returning a new list. For example, if words is ["ab", "abc", "a", "abcd"] and minLength is 3, then after the call words is ["abc", "abcd"]. Complete the method removeShort.

rubric_rows.criterion: Traverses every index of the list with bounds based on words.size()
required_elements: for (int i = 0; i < words.size(); i++) or a backward loop
common_errors: skips the first or last element

rubric_rows.criterion: Uses get(i) to read an element and length() to read its length
Tests for strings shorter than minLength with a correct boundary
Removes the element at index i (remove(i)) when the test is true
Accounts for the shift caused by a removal (backward traversal, or the index is not advanced after a removal)
required_elements: i-- or backward loop or no i++ after remove
common_errors: skips the element that moves into the removed position

rubric_rows.criterion: Does not remove elements incorrectly: every short string is removed and no other string is removed
Preserves the order of the remaining elements
Changes the original list (words) instead of building and discarding a new list
The method compiles with return type void and correct ArrayList<String> and String use
required_elements: public static void removeShort(ArrayList<String> words, int minLength)
common_errors: returns a value from a void method
